author: high
claim: The longest-trail decomposition solves the target theorem directly.
evidence: Subgoal 1 is solved by endpoint parity: a maximum-length trail cannot have different endpoints, since its terminal vertex would have an unused incident edge allowing extension. Subgoal 2 is solved by connectivity and rotation: if the resulting closed trail omitted an edge, a shortest path from an endpoint of an omitted edge to the trail would furnish an unused edge incident to a trail vertex; rotate the closed trail to that vertex and append the edge. Therefore the maximum-length trail is closed and uses every edge exactly once.

links.subgoal: Prove a maximum-length trail is closed and edge-spanning.
links.attempt_summary: Both endpoint-parity and edge-spanning subgoals are solved.

glossary.G: the finite connected undirected graph in the problem
glossary.T: a trail of maximum possible number of edges in G
glossary.V(T): the set of vertices occurring on T
